records.title: AdaptOrch: Dynamic Topology Routing via DAG Analysis
records.relevance_note: Introduces linear-time runtime DAG analysis to dynamically route subtasks into parallel, sequential, or hybrid topologies.
records.reason_included: Provides concrete thresholds (Coupling Density) for transitioning between parallel and sequential multi-agent execution.

claim_snippets.claim_text: AdaptOrch routes execution to one of four topologies based on Coupling Density, with an optimal functional threshold range of [0.55, 0.65].
Setting coupling thresholds above 0.8 allows parallel execution of tightly coupled tasks, leading to catastrophic consistency failures.

records.relevance_note: Explores fluid round-by-round rewiring of the multi-agent computation graph based on internal state needs.

claim_snippets.claim_text: DyTopo induces a sparse directed communication graph using cosine similarity between l2-normalized embeddings of agent Need and Offer descriptors.
Optimal sparsity threshold (tau) lies between [0.3, 0.4]; thresholds below 0.3 recreate the 'bag of agents' communication flooding failure.

records.relevance_note: Examines the role of formal deterministic verifiers (LEAN 4) to rescue LLMs from logic failures outside their pretraining distribution.

The harness uses deterministic compilation errors from a formal LEAN Verifier to mathematically force the LLM to refine incorrect proofs and recursively decompose subgoals.

records.title: WebWeaver: Topology Inference Attacks in LLM-MAS
records.relevance_note: Exposes a severe vulnerability where entire multi-agent routing topologies can be reverse-engineered.
records.reason_included: Mandates specific topological constraints (blinded routing) for security, impacting all future enterprise MAS designs.

claim_snippets.claim_text: An adversary can reconstruct the hidden multi-agent topology of an organization by compromising a single edge agent via a diffusion-based graph reconstruction mechanism.
Topologies must implement network-level compartmentalization via blinded routing gateways to prevent structural mapping.

records.title: Effective Strategies for Asynchronous Software Engineering Agents
records.relevance_note: Direct manager-worker topology with async branch-and-merge ablations on coding benchmarks.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete topology, communication contract, isolation primitive, and measured single-vs-multi-agent results.

claim_snippets.claim_text: CAID uses a central manager to build a dependency graph, delegate work through a machine-parsable JSON protocol, and run engineer agents concurrently in isolated git worktrees.
CAID improves accuracy over single-agent baselines by 26.7 percentage points on PaperBench and 14.3 points on Commit0-Lite.
Worktree isolation is the primitive that realizes the branch side of branch-and-merge coordination; replacing it with soft isolation collapses much of the gain toward single-agent performance.

records.relevance_note: Explicit topology guidance based on task coupling for long-running scientific coding.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A Boltzmann solver is treated as a deeply coupled pipeline where a single agent working sequentially, spawning subagents as needed, is better suited than a large parallel team.
CLAUDE.md serves as a mutable global plan kept in context, while CHANGELOG.md serves as portable long-term memory so later sessions avoid retrying failed approaches.
A Ralph-loop style orchestration pattern is used to push the agent past premature completion by re-entering context until the explicit success criterion is met.

records.title: Verified Multi-Agent Orchestration: A Plan-Execute-Verify-Replan Framework for Complex Query Resolution
records.relevance_note: Direct plan-execute-verify-replan topology with explicit DAG planner, verifier placement, and stop rules.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete topology and comparison against single-agent and static pipeline baselines.

claim_snippets.claim_text: VMAO decomposes a query into a DAG of sub-questions, executes dependency-ready nodes in parallel, and uses an orchestration-level verifier to trigger adaptive replanning.
Across 25 market-research queries, VMAO improves answer completeness from 3.1 to 4.2 and source quality from 2.6 to 4.1 versus a single-agent baseline.

Termination is governed by explicit stop conditions including completeness threshold, confidence threshold, diminishing returns, token budget, and maximum iterations; the full system uses 850K tokens versus 100K for single-agent.

records.title: Silo-Bench: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
records.relevance_note: Topology and communication-protocol benchmark exposing scale and coordination failure modes.
records.reason_included: Provides direct failure taxonomy and protocol-level evidence for coordination overhead.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Silo-Bench evaluates multi-agent coordination across three orthogonal axes—agent scale, communication protocol, and model—under parallel round-based execution.
The benchmark isolates three dominant failure modes: Premature Submission (37.2%), Consensus Failure (29.9%), and Computation Error (28.6%), which together define a communication-reasoning gap.
At larger scales, spontaneous leader emergence can hurt outcomes: on Level-III tasks runs with an emergent leader have 0.0% success versus 33.3% without one, indicating centralization bottlenecks.

records.title: DyTopo: Dynamic Topology Routing for Multi-Agent Reasoning via Semantic Matching
records.relevance_note: Direct comparison of dynamic versus fixed communication topologies for multi-round agents.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete routing mechanism, memory-update contract, and costed baseline comparisons.

claim_snippets.claim_text: DyTopo reconstructs a sparse directed communication graph every round by semantically matching each agent’s query descriptor to other agents’ key descriptors, then routes only the induced private messages.
Across code-generation and mathematical-reasoning benchmarks with four LLM backbones, DyTopo beats the strongest baseline in all 16 backbone-dataset settings with mean gain about 6.1 points.
Fixed-horizon baselines waste tokens and latency: on HumanEval, DyTopo reaches the highest accuracy while using 48% of AgentScope’s tokens and converging in 2.6 rounds on average.

records.title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
records.relevance_note: Real long-running parallel coding harness with concrete coordination primitives and failure reports.
records.reason_included: Exposes a non-orchestrated parallel topology, synchronization scheme, and where parallelism breaks.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The harness runs Claude in an infinite autonomous loop, then scales out to multiple agents by placing each in its own Docker container with a local clone of a shared bare git repository.

Coordination is implemented with lock files in current_tasks plus pull-merge-push cycles; the prototype intentionally has no orchestration agent and frequent merge conflicts are part of normal operation.

Parallelism helped when many failures were independent, but 16 agents stalled on Linux-kernel compilation because they all hit the same bottleneck; using GCC as a known-good oracle re-partitioned work and restored useful parallelism.

records.title: Scaling Multiagent Systems with Process Rewards
records.relevance_note: Topology-aware multiagent training source grounded in terminal environments and explicit specialization.
records.reason_included: Defines pre-set multiagent topologies in terminal settings and reports architecture-linked training effects.

claim_snippets.claim_text: MAPPA trains tool-augmented multiagent systems in a terminal environment where agents with separate weights execute in a pre-defined topology such as sequential pipeline, debate, or mixture-of-agents.
MAPPA uses a coach model to assign per-action process rewards based on role, observed context, action, and tool feedback, addressing inter-agent credit assignment that sparse outcome rewards miss.

On held-out tasks, MAPPA reports gains of +5.0 to +17.5 points on AIME/AMC and +12.5 points success-rate improvement on DSBench; its own analysis also finds coach-score bias can induce unwanted specialization.

records.title: When Single-Agent with Skills Replace Multi-Agent Systems and When They Fail
records.relevance_note: Direct single-agent versus multi-agent topology comparison with scaling failure analysis.
records.reason_included: Provides explicit tradeoff between external coordination and internal skill selection, plus failure threshold.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper compiles sequential multi-agent workflows into a single agent that internally invokes structured skills such as decompose, solve, and verify within one shared context window.
In the compiled setting, token consumption drops by 53.7% on average because the single agent avoids repeated cross-agent context re-encoding while maintaining competitive accuracy.

Skill selection remains stable only up to a capacity threshold; once large skill libraries are reached, accuracy drops sharply, but hierarchical routing recovers about 37-40 points for GPT-4o-mini when |S| is at least 60.

records.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
records.relevance_note: Effective harnesses for long-running agents is a engineering writeup source with details on two role topology, initializer agent relevant to agent architecture.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on topology, memory, artifacts workspace.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The harness uses a two-role topology: an initializer agent creates the initial environment, while a coding agent repeatedly resumes work in later sessions using the artifacts left behind.

The initializer writes init.sh, a progress file, and an initial git commit; later coding sessions read progress notes, git history, and a structured feature list before choosing a single next feature.

The design is explicitly aimed at failure modes where agents try to one-shot the project, leave undocumented half-finished work, or declare victory too early; the proposed mitigation is incremental work plus self-verification before marking features as passing.

records.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
records.exception_reason: Official production architecture writeup for orchestrator-worker research agents; uniquely details delegation rules, memory persistence, and parallelization failures that remain directly relevant to topology design.
records.relevance_note: How we built our multi-agent research system is a engineering writeup source with details on orchestrator worker, parallel subagents relevant to agent architecture.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on topology, execution loop, memory.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The production research system uses an orchestrator-worker topology: a lead agent plans, persists its plan to memory, spawns specialized subagents in parallel, and hands final findings to a CitationAgent.

In Anthropic’s internal research eval, a multi-agent system with Claude Opus 4 lead and Claude Sonnet 4 subagents outperformed single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2%, with token usage explaining most variance on BrowseComp.

Detailed delegation prompts and explicit scaling rules were required to prevent duplicated work and runaway subagent counts; parallelizing both subagents and tool calls cut research time by up to 90%, while synchronous lead-agent execution still created bottlenecks.
